### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-approvals`, touching **8** documentable anchor(s).

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`  _(via ApprovalService (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via canReadObject (literal, a string literal in ObjectReadAdmission))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx`  _(via canReadObject (literal, a string literal in ObjectReadAdmission))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via ApprovalService (symbol, a top-level class), canReadObject (literal, a string literal in ObjectReadAdmission))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **6** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 57994c311f4acc576e1a1eb9ad4162d191d15905` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `8a31df4b49df12fda0e391f574d82a1adbd0e49e` — the merge of head `37573fbd67a8ab04a0373248da587cb63895a17b` into base `57994c311f4acc576e1a1eb9ad4162d191d15905`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 8a31df4b49df12fda0e391f574d82a1adbd0e49e && git checkout 8a31df4b49df12fda0e391f574d82a1adbd0e49e
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 57994c311f4acc576e1a1eb9ad4162d191d15905 37573fbd67a8ab04a0373248da587cb63895a17b && git checkout -B drift-repro 57994c311f4acc576e1a1eb9ad4162d191d15905 && git merge --no-ff 37573fbd67a8ab04a0373248da587cb63895a17b

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 57994c311f4acc576e1a1eb9ad4162d191d15905
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 57994c311f4acc576e1a1eb9ad4162d191d15905` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `37573fbd67a8ab04a0373248da587cb63895a17b`
Local-runs: none

Read: card #23637 (body and all four comments: triage `6188373141`, claim `6190546282`, os-dev-report `6191744169`, regrade `6191803622`); PR #23672 body, its 5-file list and the net diff against `main` at the head (merge-base `881eeff315`, +592/-11); the 39 check-runs on the head, latest per name, read twice without waiting; #7497 ruling C (`6051659422`); `payload-redaction.ts`'s header (#10749) on the head; PR #23629's contract record (`6187371379`); PR #23663 (#23279) as landed on `main` at `94924e01c1` (`parent-record-read-gate.ts`, `audit-plugin.ts`); `resolveReadableParentIds` and `withoutOperationPrivateKeys` in `packages/core`; the `canReadObject` contract (`packages/spec/src/contracts/security-service.ts`) and plugin-security's implementation; the REST approvals routes on the head. Function level only, per the card's security gate.

### ① Derived judgments

**Accept-set and public-surface changes the diff implies, each judged.**

1. **(1) Every `payload_display` lookup-target title is now served only for a target RECORD the reader may read, on both inbox doors.** On the head, `payload_display` is set in exactly one place (`enrichRows`, the one assignment at its tail), and `enrichRows` is reached from exactly two call sites: `listRequests` and `loadRequest`, the latter being `getRequest`'s body. Both pass the `context` the request's own visibility was judged by. In `enrichRows` the order is now: the exposure gate (`servesPayloadDisplayTarget`, #22738, unchanged, first), then `admittedTargetObjects` (object-level, the reader's envelope), then `resolveReadableParentIds` (`@objectstack/core`, one caller-scoped read per admitted object, the reader's envelope), then `targets` is the admitted objects with at least one readable id, then `servedFields` (FLS, #23618, unchanged) and `titlesAsServed` with `readableIds.get(object)` in place of `refIds.get(object)`. So the system-context title read now takes only the ids the reader's own read returned; a refused object, a hidden row and a deleted record all come back absent and the stored id stands. **Right**: this is the card's point 2 as filed and as triage pre-ruled it (narrow through the platform's existing row-access door, degrade as a deleted target does), and `resolveReadableParentIds` is that door (its header: the one answer the comment, activity, ledger, attachment and mail gates ask; do not hand-copy). The code-line diff of the service is only the two imports, the two types, the field, the attach point, `admittedTargetObjects`, the four lines in `enrichRows` and the one argument change; nothing else moves.
2. **(1) No other producer of `payload_display` is left out.** A grep of `packages`, `services` and `apps` at the head finds the key produced nowhere but `enrichRows` and declared in `packages/spec`'s `ApprovalRequestRow` (optional). The two REST routes (`GET .../approvals/requests` and `.../requests/:id`) call the two doors with the `resolveExecCtx` context after `enforceAuth`. The other `getRequest` callers are `listActions` and the decision-attachment visibility check, both with the caller's context, and `resolveActionToken` under `SYSTEM_CTX`. That system read yields whole titles (plugin-security's `isSystem` bypass in `canReadObject`, and an unscoped read), but its only consumers are `peekActionToken` and `redeemActionToken`, served by the plugin's self-hosted mount through `action-link-pages.ts`, which reads `submitter_name`, `submitter_id`, `step_label`, `record_id`, `process_name`, `process_label`, `object_name`, `object_label` and `current_step` and never `payload` or `payload_display` (the word appears once, in a comment). Unchanged by this diff, and the same finding as PR #23629's record item 4. **Right.**
3. **(2) Nothing is granted, and the SUBJECT is untouched.** The only code lines changed narrow the set of target ids that are titled. `resolveSubjectDisplays`, `servedSubjectFields`, `redactPayloads`, `record_title`, `object_label` and the FLS-redacted snapshot have no code-line change; the new reads are reads (`fields: ['id']`, bounded by the id count), the exposure gate still runs first, and the target read itself (`titlesAsServed`, `SYSTEM_CTX`) is unchanged in body. A routed approver with no read on the subject record is served the subject exactly as before (pin (d) asserts `record_title`, `object_label` and `payload` equal to the control's, on both doors). What ruling C gives an approver (the inbox entry, the FLS-redacted snapshot holding the target's id, the actions) is unchanged; what the ruling keeps with object permissions, sharing and row-level rules (record access) is what is now asked of the referenced record. **Right, and the fork did not open**: the diff reads no new meaning into ruling C. The reviewer agrees with the dev and triage here: PR #23629's record called this a design decision beside ruling C and left it to a card of its own; #23637 is that card, and triage pre-ruled its fix on measurement. Nothing is widened, which is the only act the card reserves for the maintainer.
4. **(3) Fail-closed posture, and the same posture PR #23663 landed.** `admittedTargetObjects` resolves the source inside a try/catch (a throwing resolver is read as absent); a service without the optional member returns every object to step 2; an answer that is not `=== true` refuses the object; a throw refuses the object and is said once at `warn` as a fault. `admittedParentObjects` in `parent-record-read-gate.ts` at `94924e01c1` is the same shape line for line (try/catch around the resolver, `typeof canReadObject !== 'function'` as the absent state, `=== true`, warn on throw, exclude otherwise), and `approvals-plugin.ts`'s resolver is the same as `audit-plugin.ts`'s `getReadAdmission` (`ctx.getService('security')` in a try/catch returning `undefined`). **Can the absent state widen what is served?** No: with no admission, every exposed object goes to `resolveReadableParentIds` as the reader, which is the reader-scoped read alone; the admission only removes objects from that set, and by the contract (`canReadObject` is the middleware's own object-level arms, computed from the same resolution) an object it refuses is one the reader-scoped read would have refused. So the served set under absence equals the reader-scoped read's, and under presence is a subset of it. A reader whose envelope carries no principal is refused by both (ADR-0096 D5 in `canReadObject`; the middleware's principal-less refusal on the read), so an undefined context closes too; the REST doors never reach here unauthenticated. The two reads a refused object would otherwise log (#23279's interplay) are avoided without muting, catching or lowering any log: the dev measured 1 WARN per refused object per read without the admission and 0 with it, and nothing in plugin-security changes. **Right.**
5. **(4) The reader's envelope is the one the request was judged by; no second derivation.** `listRequests` and `getRequest` take the `resolveAuthzContext` envelope (the #7135 full-envelope note at the file's head), judge the request's visibility by it (`actingCaller`, `visibleRequestIds`) and hand the same `context` object to `enrichRows`. `admittedTargetObjects` asks `canReadObject` with `withoutOperationPrivateKeys(context)` copied, and `resolveReadableParentIds` sends the same strip of the same `context`; neither rebuilds a session or re-derives permissions, and the strip drops only the `__` operation-private widening keys, in the safe direction `operation-private-keys.ts` documents. Pin (e) asserts the admission is asked with `permissions`, `positions` and `userId` and without a `__readScope` the caller carried. **Right.** The `approvals-plugin.ts` wiring line is within the claim's purpose: route-and-surface rule 2 (a capability the host should get is mounted explicitly); without it the admission is dead in the composed runtime (ablation D, pin (f)); it is one lazy resolver beside the field-visibility one, the same shape PR #23629's record accepted at its judgment 8 and the shape `audit-plugin.ts` landed at `94924e01c1`; the dev declared it in the PR body and the report. **Right.**
6. **(4) The two new exported types are not a public-surface change.** `ObjectReadAdmission` (a Pick of `ISecurityService`'s `canReadObject`) and `ObjectReadAdmissionSource` are exported from the module `approval-service.ts` only. `index.ts` re-exports from that module by a named list that does not include them (verified on the head), and `package.json`'s `exports` map is `.` only, served from `dist/index.*`, so they are package-private, as `ParentObjectReadAdmission` is in plugin-audit. `attachObjectReadAdmission` is a new public method on the exported `ApprovalService` class, additive and optional (an unattached service reads as before); a new optional attach point on a service class is within patch for this package, as `attachFieldVisibility` was. **Right; semver unaffected.**
7. **Test accept-set changes.** `implicit-reference-target-lookup.test.ts`'s one pin now asserts the two `sys_user` reads that happen for an implicit `user` lookup: the reader's row-access ask (not system) and then the system title read, in that order. **Right**: it states the new accept set for the implicit-target class (a `user` lookup follows the reader's row access to `sys_user`, as `$expand` on it would). The new pin file drives the real service and the real `ApprovalsServicePlugin.start()` on a real engine over sqlite with one middleware per business object standing in for the security middleware's two answers (a refusal, a narrowed result): (a) three denial classes on both doors, equal to a deleted target's shape, the stored id standing, the titles absent from the serialised row; (a-row) per record, not per object; (b) control; (c) one row-access ask per target object per read naming every id; (d) the subject untouched; (e) admission attached: a refused object not read as the reader, an admitted one still narrowed by row, one ask per object without the `__` keys; (e-closed) throw and non-true refuse, a service without the member reads as before; (f) composed wiring. Red-before (3 failed / 2 passed, the predicted set) and four restore-proven ablations with predicted sets equal to observed are reported; not re-run here. The real-`SecurityPlugin` measurement (before: served on both doors for a row-rule class and a no-object-read class; after: withheld, a readable row of the same object keeps its title) is the card's point 1 and is reported; its finding agrees with the source read here.

**Check-runs on the head, as read (latest per name, 39 runs, read twice, not waited for):** 29 completed success, among them Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Build Core, every Lint family, every Type Check family, Dogfood Regression Gate, Test Core (5/6) and (6/6), both claim guards, the single-writer guard and the Part-of guard; 6 skipped by design (Build Docs, Console Pin Gate, Dogfood matrix shard, Dogfood Verify CLI, Packed-tarball smoke, Temporal Conformance). **In progress at both reads: Test Core (1/6), (2/6), (3/6), (4/6).** None failed. The queue's every-check-green condition is the seat's to read at landing time; this verdict is on the contract.

### ② Semver level

Changeset `.changeset/23637-lookup-target-title-row-access.md`: `@objectstack/plugin-approvals` **patch**. **Matches the diff.** The package name matches `package.json`. Nothing published moves: no `packages/spec` file is touched; `ApprovalRequestRow.payload_display` is already optional on the contract, so an absent key is within the declared shape; `enrichRows`, `admittedTargetObjects`, `titlesAsServed` and `servedFields` are private; the two new types are package-private (judgment 6); the new attach point is additive and optional; no route, query parameter, error code, translation key, notification field or export changes; nothing in `packages/core`, `plugin-security` or `plugin-audit` changes. A narrowing of served values is patch. `skip-changeset` does not apply and was not used. Check Changeset is green.

`Clause-②: no` is on the PR body, the changeset and the claim, and all three agree with the diff: no published schema or public surface is declared or changed. Right.

Governed surfaces: none in the 5-file list (no `docs/adr/**`, `.claude/**`, `skills/**`, `.github/workflows/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/NORTH-STAR.md`). The Governed Surface Queue Guard is green. The branch's two `origin/main` merges before opening touched `.claude/**` and `scripts/pm/**` on `main`'s side only; the net diff against the merge-base `881eeff315` is the 5 files.

### ③ Boundary flags

**`open_questions`: empty.** Nothing to answer.

**Deviation 1** (file surface beyond the claim's `approval-service.ts` and its tests: the one wiring call in `approvals-plugin.ts`). Answered: within purpose (judgment 5); declared in the PR body and the report; the claim's reserved paths (`packages/core`, `plugin-audit`, `plugin-security`) are untouched, as the file list shows. Within surface.

**Deviation 2** (a throwaway measurement file in this package's tree importing plugin-security's source by relative path, run three times and deleted, never committed). Answered: the net diff carries no such file and no relative cross-package import, so nothing of it ships; the measurement is what the card's point 1 asked for first, and its finding agrees with the source read here (judgment 7). No contract effect.

**Deviation 3** (push order: the pins and the fix went up together after the empty-branch probe). Answered: the card's security rule that nothing red lands on the remote before the fix governs; no contract effect.

**Deviation 4** (gates run under `os-verify-lock` as dispatched; one batch-wrapper timeout on `check:type-check-debt`, re-run to completion at exit 0). Answered: a process note; the check-runs on the head are the gate verdicts of record (Type Check · debt ledger is green). No contract effect.

**Deviation 5** (two `origin/main` merges before opening; the package suite not re-run after them). Answered: the merge-base is `881eeff315` and the net diff is the 5 files (section ②); the head's Build Core, every Type Check family and Test Core (5/6) and (6/6) are green, the remaining Test Core shards in progress at read time. No contract effect.

**Deviation 6** (model-free commit trailers and the repository's session footer). Answered: a process note with no contract effect; the repository's instructions govern the seat.

**`out_of_scope_findings` entry 1: `submitter_name` and `pending_approver_names` are read under the system context (`resolveUserNames`, `sys_user` by id and by email, fields id, name, email).** Judged: **not a defect this card names, and not a disclosure of the class this card names; the PR is complete on the card's terms.** The card names a lookup target in the payload snapshot, a referenced business record whose title the snapshot never stored. The participant names belong to the inbox entry itself, which ruling C gives the approver (who submitted, who is still pending), and the entry is already tenant-scoped by `buildRequestWhere` and `findRequestRow`. Whether a directory name should be served to a reader who holds no read on `sys_user` at all is the same shape of question as this card's, for a different object and a different class of consumer; if the seat wants it settled it is a card of its own, filed with a measurement first, not an incompleteness of this PR. The seat decides any filing.

**`out_of_scope_findings` entry 2: a lookup pointing at the request's own subject record now follows the reader's row access to that record, while `record_title` is served regardless.** Judged: **not a defect, and not a disclosure.** Both values are the same record's title, picked by the same `titlesAsServed` and the same served-fields answer (a target that is also the subject object reuses the subject's answer); withholding the copy in `payload_display` discloses nothing the row does not already carry in `record_title`, and serving `record_title` is ruling C's text. A self-lookup to a DIFFERENT record of the subject object (pin (a)'s third class) is correctly withheld. A parity oddity in the row shape, not a contract question; nothing to file.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-23637-lookup-target-row-access`
Reviewed-by: `session_017WLmd5in9RXu7AjyHR8fKQ`

**VERDICT: PASS**
